questions.questionText: Which method should you use inside build() to reactively listen to provider changes?
questions.explanation: ref.watch() subscribes the widget to updates and rebuilds it when the state changes.

questions.questionText: What is the primary benefit of Clean Architecture in Flutter apps?
options: Decouples UI and business logic so backends can be swapped easily
Eliminates the need for any state management package
questions.explanation: Clean Architecture strictly separates UI from data sources, allowing seamless backend swaps.

questions.questionText: Which Riverpod provider type is recommended for managing asynchronous states?
questions.explanation: AsyncNotifierProvider handles AsyncValue (loading, data, error) cleanly and safely.

questions.questionText: Where should API calls and Dio requests be executed?
options: Directly inside the build method of widgets
questions.explanation: DataSources are strictly responsible for network and database interactions.

questions.questionText: What does the autoDispose modifier do in Riverpod?
options: Automatically cancels state and releases memory when no longer listened to
Permanently saves state to local storage
Restarts the app when an error occurs
questions.explanation: autoDispose frees up resources as soon as the widget listening to the provider unmounts.

questions.questionText: Which CSS property defines alignment along the main axis in Flexbox?
questions.explanation: justify-content aligns items along the primary flex axis.

questions.questionText: What is the default flex-direction of a flex container?
questions.explanation: By default, flex-direction is row.

questions.questionText: In CSS Grid, what unit represents a fraction of the available space?
questions.explanation: The fr unit represents a fraction of free grid container space.

questions.questionText: Which property creates space between grid tracks or flex items?
questions.explanation: gap defines the gutter between grid rows/columns or flex items.

questions.questionText: What media query feature is used for mobile-first responsive breakpoints?
questions.explanation: Mobile-first design utilizes min-width queries to progressively enhance larger screens.

questions.questionText: Which join returns only matching records from both tables?
questions.explanation: INNER JOIN selects rows having matching values in both tables.

questions.questionText: Which clause filters records after grouping with GROUP BY?
questions.explanation: HAVING filters aggregate results produced by GROUP BY.

questions.questionText: What does ACID stand for in database transaction theory?
questions.explanation: ACID guarantees database reliability: Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, Durability.

questions.questionText: What type of index is most commonly used in PostgreSQL for equality and range queries?
questions.explanation: B-Tree is the default and most versatile index type in relational databases.

questions.questionText: Which normal form eliminates transitive functional dependencies?
questions.explanation: Third Normal Form (3NF) requires 2NF and that no non-prime attribute transitively depends on the primary key.

questions.questionText: Why are NumPy operations significantly faster than standard Python lists?
options: They are implemented in C with contiguous memory storage
They only work with text strings
questions.explanation: NumPy stores elements contiguously and executes vectorized operations in compiled C.

questions.questionText: What function creates an identity matrix in NumPy?
questions.explanation: np.eye(N) returns an N x N 2-D array with ones on the diagonal and zeros elsewhere.

questions.questionText: What is array broadcasting in NumPy?
options: Sending array data over a network socket
Operating on arrays of different shapes under compatible dimensions
questions.explanation: Broadcasting describes how NumPy treats arrays with different shapes during arithmetic operations.

questions.questionText: Which method returns the dimensions of an ndarray?
questions.explanation: .shape returns a tuple of integers indicating the size of the array along each axis.

questions.questionText: What Pandas method drops rows with null values?
questions.explanation: df.dropna() removes rows containing missing or NaN values.

questions.questionText: What algorithm is used to compute gradients in neural networks via the chain rule?
questions.explanation: Backpropagation computes the gradient of the loss function with respect to weights using the chain rule.

questions.questionText: Which activation function maps values to a probability distribution between 0 and 1 summing to 1?
questions.explanation: Softmax turns raw logits into a normalized probability distribution over multiple classes.

questions.questionText: What is the purpose of a validation dataset in machine learning?
options: To train the final weights of the model
To tune hyperparameters and detect overfitting before testing
To store backups of the model
questions.explanation: The validation set provides an unbiased evaluation while tuning model hyperparameters.

questions.questionText: What issue occurs when gradients become exponentially small in deep networks?
questions.explanation: Vanishing gradients prevent early layers from learning effectively in deep architectures.

questions.questionText: What does CNN stand for in deep learning?
questions.explanation: CNN stands for Convolutional Neural Network, typically used for spatial and visual recognition.

questions.questionText: How do Java Virtual Threads differ from traditional platform threads?
options: They are lightweight user-mode threads managed by the JVM rather than OS threads
They do not allow network calls
They are limited to 10 threads max
questions.explanation: Virtual threads are lightweight JVM-managed threads, allowing millions of concurrent tasks with minimal overhead.

questions.questionText: Which keyword creates an immutable data carrier class in Java 16+?
questions.explanation: record classes in Java are transparent holders for immutable data.

questions.questionText: Which collection does NOT preserve the insertion order of elements?
questions.explanation: HashSet does not make any guarantees as to the iteration order of the elements.

questions.questionText: What is the purpose of the Optional<T> class in Java?
options: To explicitly represent the presence or absence of a value, avoiding NullPointerExceptions
questions.explanation: Optional provides a clear API to handle nullable returns safely.

questions.questionText: Which functional interface in java.util.function takes one argument and returns a boolean?
questions.explanation: Predicate<T> represents a predicate (boolean-valued function) of one argument.

questions.questionText: What is the correct sequence of the standard TCP three-way handshake?
questions.explanation: TCP establishes connections using SYN -> SYN-ACK -> ACK.

questions.questionText: On which OSI layer does IP (Internet Protocol) operate?
questions.explanation: IP is a Layer 3 Network layer protocol responsible for routing.

questions.questionText: Which protocol is connectionless and does NOT guarantee packet delivery or order?
questions.explanation: UDP provides fast, unreliable, connectionless datagram delivery.

questions.questionText: What standard port does HTTPS utilize by default?
questions.explanation: Port 443 is the standard port for TLS/HTTPS encrypted web traffic.

questions.questionText: What type of attack floods a target with traffic to exhaust its resources?
questions.explanation: Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) overwhelms bandwidth or computational capacity.

questions.questionText: In a stateless REST API with JWT, what should the SessionCreationPolicy be set to in Spring Security?
questions.explanation: SessionCreationPolicy.STATELESS ensures Spring does not maintain an HTTP session.

questions.questionText: What standard HTTP header is used to pass the Bearer JWT token in requests?
questions.explanation: The Authorization header formatted as "Bearer <token>" is the standard.

questions.questionText: What are the three components of a JSON Web Token separated by periods?
questions.explanation: A JWT consists of Header (algorithm), Payload (claims), and Signature (cryptographic verification).

questions.questionText: Which Spring annotation marks a class as providing bean definitions for application context?
questions.explanation: @Configuration indicates that a class declares one or more @Bean methods.

questions.questionText: Which Spring Data interface provides built-in pagination and sorting out of the box?
questions.explanation: JpaRepository extends PagingAndSortingRepository, providing full CRUD with pagination.

questions.questionText: Why should package manager install commands and cache cleanups be chained in a single RUN instruction?
options: Because Docker only supports one RUN command
To prevent leftover cache files from being committed into intermediate image layers
To speed up CPU processing during execution
questions.explanation: Each RUN creates an immutable layer; cleaning caches in the same command minimizes final image size.

questions.questionText: What is the purpose of multi-stage Docker builds?
options: To separate the build environment from the lean runtime image
To publish images to multiple registries
questions.explanation: Multi-stage builds allow compiling in heavy build environments and copying only artifacts to minimal images.

questions.questionText: Which Docker directive defines the default executable to run when the container starts?
questions.explanation: ENTRYPOINT specifies the command that will always be executed when the container starts.

questions.questionText: What is used in Docker to persist data independently of the container lifecycle?
questions.explanation: Volumes are stored on the host filesystem and persist beyond container deletion.

questions.questionText: What file excludes files and directories from the Docker build context?
questions.explanation: .dockerignore prevents unnecessary files from being sent to the Docker daemon.

questions.questionText: What is the average time complexity of searching an element in a balanced Binary Search Tree?
questions.explanation: Each step cuts the remaining search space in half, resulting in logarithmic O(log N) time.

questions.questionText: What is the worst-case search complexity in an unbalanced degenerate BST (linked list shape)?
questions.explanation: When a BST degenerates into a linear chain, searching takes O(N) linear time.

questions.questionText: Which tree traversal yields elements in sorted non-decreasing order for a BST?
questions.explanation: Inorder traversal visits Left -> Root -> Right, which visits nodes in ascending order.

questions.questionText: What data structure is typically used to implement Breadth-First Search (BFS)?
questions.explanation: BFS uses a FIFO Queue to visit all nodes level by level.

questions.questionText: What is the time complexity of QuickSort in the average case?
questions.explanation: QuickSort runs in O(N log N) average time with efficient in-place partitioning.
